We got no templates with those criteria. Maybe the template ID is 84231 but not in DB; perhaps we need to retrieve via get_template with numeric ID? Already did. Could be that the template is stored but we need to use apply_template with the mapped_rxn? Actually the input from template_search gave mapped_rxn: 'COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(C[NH+]4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1>>COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1' This is forward reaction? It shows product (with C[NH+]4CC(F)C4) to reactant (with CCl). So the template is the transformation of CCl to C[NH+]4... So we could extract the reaction SMARTS from mapped_rxn? The mapped_rxn is not mapped but just SMILES of product>>reactant. We need a retrosynthetic template that when applied to target (product) yields precursors: the product is the molecule with C[NH+]4... Actually the initial molecule is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1 which contains CN4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine with positive charge). The mapped_rxn shows product (with that amine) >> reactant (with CCl). So the retrosynthetic step is to replace the amine side chain with a chlorophenyl side chain. So the precursors would be: the aryl chloride (the phenyl with CCl) and the amine (maybe the amine part?). Actually the reaction is intramolecular? The product has a side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the heterocycle. The reactant has Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3. So the transformation is substitution of the side chain: the phenyl ring attached to heterocycle via a CH2 (C) then phenyl with substituent (Cl vs N4...). So the SN2 is on the substituent on phenyl? Actually the side chain is a phenyl ring with a substituent at para position: either Cl (leaving group) or N4CC(F)C4 (nucleophile). So the retrosynthetic step would break the C-N bond (between phenyl carbon and N4...), forming C-Cl bond, generating two fragments: the phenyl chloride (CCl) and the amine fragment (N4CC(F)C4). So the precursors are: the aryl chloride (CCl) and the amine (N4CC(F)C4). But also the rest of the molecule remains unchanged. So the precursor set likely is: [product without side chain? Actually the rest of molecule is the same, just the side chain changes. So the precursor molecules are: the core scaffold (the rest of molecule) with a hydrogen at that position? But typical retrosynthetic template would cut the bond and give two fragments: the core (with a leaving group placeholder) and the nucleophile. However the template may produce two fragments: the core with a halide (CCl) and the amine (N4CC(F)C4). The core with CCl is the same as the reactant given: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1. That's the whole molecule with CCl. The amine fragment is maybe [N4CC(F)C4] as a separate molecule? Actually the amine is attached via CH2 to phenyl: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. The nucleophile is N4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine). In SN2, the nucleophile is the amine (maybe as a free amine). So the precursor set: [COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1, N4CC(F)C4] but the amine is attached to phenyl via CH2? Wait the nucleophile is CN4..., which is attached to phenyl carbon. In SN2, the nucleophile attacks the carbon bearing Cl, displacing Cl, forming C-N bond. So the nucleophile is the amine (maybe as a free amine). The leaving group is Cl. So the precursors: the aryl chloride (the whole molecule with CCl) and the amine (maybe as a separate small molecule). However the amine is attached to CH2? Actually the nucleophile is the amine attached to CH2? The nucleophile is the amine group (N4CC(F)C4) which is attached to CH2 group that is part of the side chain. In the product, the CH2 is attached to phenyl and to N4... So the nucleophile is the amine with a CH2? The SN2 reaction would be between the phenyl carbon (bearing Cl) and the amine's carbon? This is confusing.

But perhaps the template will produce two fragments: the core scaffold with a halide (the whole molecule) and the amine fragment (N4CC(F)C4). Let's try to apply the template using the mapped_rxn as a SMARTS? Could use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching? Not needed.

Maybe we can directly construct the precursor list manually: The target molecule is the product (with amine). The precursor set is: 1) the same molecule but with Cl instead of the amine side chain (the core with CCl). That's the SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1. 2) the amine fragment: N4CC(F)C4? But that is a positively charged tertiary amine? In the product, it's [N+H]4? Actually the SMILES in mapped_rxn: C[NH+]4CC(F)C4. That's a protonated amine. The free amine would be CN4CC(F)C4? Actually the side chain is C[NH+]4CC(F)C4 (a quaternary ammonium?). The amine is N4CC(F)C4 with a positive charge on N. The nucleophile could be the neutral amine (maybe N4CC(F)C4). But we can provide the SMILES as N4CC(F)C4 (neutral). However the template may expect the charged version. Let's use the SMILES from mapped_rxn: C[NH+]4CC(F)C4 (the fragment attached to phenyl). But as a separate molecule, that would be [NH+]4? Actually the SMILES includes the carbon attached to phenyl: C[NH+]4CC(F)C4. That includes the CH2 attached to phenyl (C). If we separate, the fragment would be C[NH+]4CC(F)C4 (a cation). So the precursor list: ['COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1', 'C[NH+]4CC(F)C4'].

But there might be alternative precursors: maybe the amine could be provided as the neutral amine CN4CC(F)C4 (without charge). Also the leaving group could be Cl as separate? But the core already includes Cl.

Thus answer list of lists: one combination.

Return: [['COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1', 'C[NH+]4CC(F)C4']]

Let's provide that.
